About.title: About Tachawit
About.lead: A place to learn, hear and keep the Amazigh language of the Aurès.
About.story1: Tachawit is spoken by the Chaoui people of the Aurès mountains, from Batna and Khenchela to Oum El Bouaghi, Tébessa and Biskra. It is mostly passed on by voice, at home, and there is very little to learn it from online.
About.story2: This project starts from those voices. The words and phrases are recorded with native speakers in Merouana, and every lesson is built around listening: short, playful steps, a map of the region to travel through, and a daily review so words stay.
About.story3: It is also a community project. Families, teachers and anyone who speaks Tachawit can add words, local variants and recordings, so that the language of every village has its place.

voices.body: Every word is heard from a native speaker, with consent recorded for each voice.
